title: Powering Prosperity: The Impact of Intuit’s Elevate Grant Program
summary: Discover how Intuit's Elevate Grant Program invested $250,000 in 25 grassroots nonprofits across LA, San Diego, and Atlanta to power community prosperity.

- Powering Prosperity: The Impact of Intuit’s Elevate Grant Program


At Intuit, our mission is to power prosperity for the people and communities we serve. That starts with investing in the places where we live and work. Through Elevate, our $250,000 microgrant program, we provided 25 nonprofit organizations across Los Angeles, San Diego, and Atlanta with $10,000 each in unrestricted funding to advance economic mobility in their communities. These organizations are expanding access to technology and education, supporting entrepreneurship, and opening doors to new careers. The grants helped expand academic coaching for more than 1,100 students, create pathways into union construction trades and clean energy careers, and amplify the stories of underrepresented artists and entrepreneurs shaping their neighborhoods.


## **How Elevate Began: 200 Conversations in Los Angeles**


Elevate’s roots are in Los Angeles, where our team connected with more than 200 local leaders and organizations across the city — conversations that surfaced extraordinary work already underway, and an opportunity for Intuit to help strengthen it through meaningful investment.


That insight shaped the Intuit Elevate Grant Program, built to:


1. **Foster economic mobility** — invest in community-driven organizations that help break down financial barriers and build local economic mobility.
2. **Support community-led solutions** — back a diverse range of initiatives designed by the people closest to their communities’ needs.
3. **Build & connect opportunity** — connect community leaders with opportunities.


Our support also helps organizations advance priorities that align with[Intuit’s goal of equipping 50 million students with financial education by 2030.](https://www.intuit.com/blog/social-responsibility/job-readiness/financial-literacy-in-a-class-of-its-own/) Together, these efforts deepen our commitment beyond funding, building lasting partnerships rooted in local needs.


Across Los Angeles, San Diego, and Atlanta, our 25 partner organizations are putting these grants into action by expanding STEM education, supporting entrepreneurship, strengthening financial literacy, developing young leaders, and closing the digital divide. Meet the changemakers creating new opportunities in their communities.


## **Driving Workforce & Technology Education in Los Angeles**


Our Los Angeles cohort represents a dynamic cross-section of leaders expanding educational access, digital equity, and community health across Southern California. The Elevate grantees are connecting Angelenos to education, employment, and economic mobility.[i.am College Track](http://i.am/) provided academic coaching and career preparation for more than 1,100 scholars, while[New Village Girls Academy](https://newvillagegirlsacademy.org/) reported a 91% senior graduation rate, with 83% of graduates enrolling in college.


For adults seeking a fresh start,[Flintridge Center’s](https://www.flintridge.org/) Apprenticeship Preparation Program served 106 formerly incarcerated adults and reported a 10% recidivism rate, compared with 47% countywide. Grantees are also supporting entrepreneurs and small businesses:[TEC Leimert’s](https://tecleimert.org/) NXT LVL Biz helped 30 small businesses strengthen their marketing, while[New Economics for Women’s](https://neweconomicsforwomen.org/) programs reached more than 6,000 business owners and supported members by connecting them to over 4,500 jobs. Together, these organizations are linking education and workforce preparation with the resources people need to build careers, grow businesses, strengthen financial literacy, and achieve greater economic mobility.


> > *“What sets the Intuit Elevate Grant apart isn’t just the funding—it’s the people behind it. The Elevate team shows up for their grantees in a way that’s rare. They’re genuinely accessible, they listen, and they’ve built real community among the organizations they support. Being connected to other grantees doing this work has been just as valuable as the grant itself.”*
> >
> >
> > Paris McCoy, Executive Director, TEC Leimert

## **Sustainability and Community Leadership in San Diego**


In San Diego, Elevate grantees are creating opportunities through workforce development, environmental stewardship, cultural representation, and youth empowerment.[The Arc of San Diego](https://www.arc-sd.com/) used its grant to support job coaching and vocational training for individuals with disabilities.[GRID Alternatives San Diego](https://gridalternatives.org/) expanded access to no-cost solar energy and training for careers in clean energy.[MANA de San Diego](https://manasd.org/) supported its Hermanitas Youth Mentorship Program for young Latinas, reporting that 100% of participating seniors graduated high school on time.[ECOLIFE](https://www.ecolifeconservation.org/) Conservation sustained its Aquaponics Innovation Center and partnership with the Viejas Band, donating approximately 630 pounds of produce and repairing a storm-damaged greenhouse.[Chicano Federation](https://www.chicanofed.org/) revitalized the Barrio Station facility, enrolling 148 youth with an average daily attendance to their program of 40. Together, these organizations are helping residents build skills, access resources, and strengthen their communities.

## **Cultivating Creativity and Next-Gen Leadership in Atlanta**


In Atlanta, Elevate grantees are nurturing creativity and opening doors for the next generation through music education, digital storytelling, and arts journalism.[Atlanta Music Project](https://atlantamusicproject.org/) used its grant to fund teaching artists with necessary materials, helping bring music education to 553 K–12 students in underserved neighborhoods. The program reported a 95% satisfaction rate, and all 22 of its seniors graduated on time.


[RE:IMAGINE](https://reimagineatl.com/) provided film and media career training to more than 200 young people, connected 28 members to job placements, and paid participants $107,000 through on-the-job learning opportunities.[ArtsATL](https://www.artsatl.org/) used its grant to spread the word about their non-profit and expand news coverage of the city’s arts community by 100 stories, contributing to 802,000 pageviews, a 28% increase over the previous year. Together, these organizations are helping young people build creative careers and bringing greater visibility to Atlanta’s artists and cultural community.

## **How to get involved**


We are proud to champion these 25 organizations and the leaders driving impact in their communities every day. Please visit their websites and check out how you can support their efforts.


If you know a nonprofit in the US, they may be eligible for Intuit’s donation program through[TechSoup](https://www.techsoup.org/intuit) , which provides Intuit QuickBooks Online to help nonprofits manage their finances.


As part of our continued commitment to empowering small businesses where we live and work, we encourage you to check out the[Intuit IDEAS Program](https://www.intuit.com/company/corporate-responsibility/intuit-ideas/) — a 12-month business accelerator offering free technology tools, coaching, and financial grants to small business owners. The new cycle is officially underway and now accepting applications through October 15th, 2026.[Apply today or explore other initiatives here.](https://www.intuit.com/company/corporate-responsibility/intuit-ideas/)
